title: Allergies: when the body overreacts
examples: What is the difference between being sick and having an allergy?
How does the immune system usually fight germs?
Can allergies affect more than just your nose?

explain.say: Today we learn about allergies and how the body reacts.

items: Allergies happen when the body overreacts.
It is not usually a sign of sickness.
The reaction is to something harmless.

explain.say: Your immune system is your body's natural defence force.
Normally, the immune system fights off germs like bacteria or viruses.
Allergens are things that trigger an allergic reaction in some people.
When the immune system mistakes an allergen for a threat, it overreacts.
A key chemical involved is histamine, which causes many allergy symptoms.

faq.q: Why do allergies make you sneeze?
faq.a: Sneezing is a reflex action to clear irritants from your nose. Histamine causes the nasal passages to swell, triggering the sneeze.
asks: Why does my nose feel blocked up?

faq.q: Are allergies the same as having a cold?
faq.a: No, a cold is usually caused by a virus, while an allergy is an immune system overreaction to something harmless like pollen.
asks: Is an allergy a type of infection?
What is the difference between sickness and allergy?

faq.q: Can I get allergies from eating certain foods?
faq.a: Yes, some people are allergic to foods like nuts. This is because the immune system reacts strongly to the proteins in the food.
asks: Why do some people react to peanuts?

faq.a: An allergen is any substance that causes an allergic reaction in a sensitive person. Common examples include pollen, dust, and certain foods.
asks: Give me an example of an allergen.

faq.a: Histamine is a chemical released by the body during an allergic reaction. It causes symptoms like itching, sneezing, and swelling.

facts: The immune system normally defends against pathogens like bacteria.
Allergens are substances that trigger an immune overreaction.
Histamine is a chemical that causes symptoms like itching.
Symptoms can include sneezing, itchy eyes, and swelling.

quiz.say: If the immune system mistakes pollen for a dangerous germ, what is the result?
quiz.why: The immune system reacts too strongly to something harmless.

wrong.1: This is wrong because the immune system always reacts to something.
wrong.2: This is wrong because the reaction itself causes symptoms first.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the mistake is the overproduction of chemicals, not the neutralization.

quiz.say: Which chemical is primarily responsible for causing symptoms like itching and swelling during an allergy?
quiz.why: Histamine is the specific chemical messenger released during the allergic response.

wrong.0: T-cells are part of the defence system, not the main symptom chemical.
wrong.1: Pathogens are the germs that the body usually fights off.
wrong.3: Antibodies are usually meant to fight germs, not cause allergy symptoms.

quiz.say: A person touches dust and has sneezing. This is an example of:
quiz.why: The reaction to dust, which is an allergen, shows the body overreacting.

wrong.1: A cold is usually caused by a virus, not just dust.
wrong.2: Failure would mean no reaction, but sneezing shows a strong reaction.
wrong.3: It is not normal because the trigger (dust) is harmless.
